name: Attainable End Corners Force Retention in a Four-Vertex Path Reduction
statement: Let an active-coordinate reduction be the path $a-b-c-d$, with lifts $a_0,a_1$. If some $a_i$ is both a geometric corner and an attainable endpoint, the family peels to the whole edge $\{a_0,a_1\}$. More generally, if both lifts are attainable but their edge cannot be retained, there are disjoint exclusive-prefix sets $R_0,R_1$ in components of their respective layers such that each can be deleted while retaining the path, each $A_i=A\setminus R_i$ peels to $a$, but $A_*=A\setminus(R_0\cup R_1)$ is ample with $a$ a leaf and does not peel to $a$. In such a failure neither lift is a geometric corner.
proof: Under nonretention, any endpoint order must first break the fibre over $a$; breaking the opposite end would leave a star reduction, and an internal path vertex cannot project from the first doubled corner. Exclusive corner tests depend only on their own complement component, so the layer-specific prefixes from the two endpoint orders can be reordered, omitted, and concatenated. Each prefix removes all exterior neighbours of $a$ in its layer. A geometric attainable lift would therefore lead after the opposite prefix to a leaf contraction peeling to $a$, from which star transfer retains the edge. Combining both prefixes gives the stated ample intersection, whose failure at $a$ is necessary to avoid the same conclusion.
